utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, at this stage, you are entitled to make your Opening Statement, in accordance with Rule 84, or you may defer making this statement until after the Prosecution's case. What do you wish to do?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because of all that was said at the opening of this hearing, I think it is quite clear that we will not be making our Opening Statement now. We will do that when the Prosecution completes its case because, by then, we will be better prepared to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Does your client wish to make a statement according to Rule 84(B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence at this moment, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. My client will not be making a statement according to Rule 84(B).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just ask Your Honour to be able to make a short comment after my colleague, Mr. Seric, makes his statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Seric, you wish to make the Opening Statement on behalf of your client now, or do you prefer to defer the Defence Opening Statement pursuant to Rule 84?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Your Excellency, the Defence of Vinko Martinovic has chosen, according to Rule 84, to make its Opening Statement after the Prosecution completes its case and before the beginning of the Defence case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you discuss your client with the right of his making a statement according to the Rule 84(B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence? What's his choice?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, we have spoken to our client, and he has chosen to adopt this same position, that is, after the completion of the Prosecution case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. But I want you not to be under any misunderstanding. Your client may make a statement right now. He cannot defer his right to the later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He will not be making a statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Krsnik, what are you going to inform the Trial Chamber at this moment? Are you going to challenge the Opening Statement by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, that was not what I had in mind. This will come in due time, and I hope we'll be able to do it very successfully. I wanted to make a comment, but I've decided against it because perhaps it will not be an appropriate time to make this comment. Maybe a more appropriate time will arise later on. The comment had to do with the witnesses. Once the actual case begins, there may be a moment that would be more opportune for me to make that comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Mr. Scott, are you ready for your first witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we are prepared to proceed, and Mr. Stringer will handle the first witness. Mr. Jan Van Hecke.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Would the usher please bring in the first witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, good afternoon, and good afternoon to Your Honours. I'm Douglas Stringer. May I suggest, Mr. President, that before the witness is brought in, there is a little bit of logistics which might be taken care of before the witness is brought in. For example, I would ask that the ELMO be moved over next to the witness place, because he is going to be looking at some things on the ELMO. And in addition, Mr. President, with this witness, if I may just take this opportunity to inform you specifically what we intend to do, which might be of help. This witness is first going to present the Trial Chamber with a series of videotape images and photographs of many of the places now which were referred to by Mr. Scott in his opening statement. And those photographs, as well as a number of the maps which Mr. Scott referred to, have been placed into binders, and what I would propose to do at this time is to distribute one of those binders to each of the Judges so that you will have each of those materials, photographs, maps, in front of you while Mr. Van Hecke is testifying. And if I could just follow that up, I don't think we'll get to it today, but tomorrow Mr. Van Hecke will also be -- through him, the Prosecutor will be tendering a number of documents into evidence. And with Mr. Van Hecke, I propose to examine a limited number of those documents, not all of them. And those documents have also been collected into binders which were prepared to provide to the Trial Chamber. And again, it may be on the theory, the hope, that it would assist you in following the testimony, to have the documents themselves in front of you, rather than having to read what's on the ELMO all the time. So we could distribute those documents to the Trial Chamber now also. Or, because I'm quite confident that we won't get into the documents today, we could simply wait, and then give you the binders of the documents tomorrow morning. On that question, Mr. President, I'm in your hands. But at the very least, I would propose now to distribute to the Trial Chamber what is called Binder 1, which contains photographs and maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I believe the Registrar has those. These would be the binders which are expressly called Binder Number 1. And inside each of those, there are photographs and maps. And for the record, Mr. President, this Binder 1 was distributed or provided to our colleagues on the Defence side some weeks ago during the deposition procedure. I believe that they have had some time to review all of those materials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. Would you please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I shall speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, you may sit down. Mr. Stringer, before you examine your witness, I think you have to remind your witness of speaking very slowly so that we could catch every word he said, since you are speaking in the same language.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I will indeed do that, Mr. President. We discussed the importance of speaking slowly during the lunch break earlier today, and I believe that the witness understands that it's important for both of us to speak, to stop, to wait, and then to continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Van Hecke, could you tell us, please, where you are currently employed.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: For the moment, I'm the head of mission for ICTY's Sarajevo field office in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: ICTY, that's the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: That's the Tribunal unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How long have you been employed as the head of mission at the Sarajevo field office?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: I started to work there in the beginning of June this year.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And prior to that time, were you here in The Hague as an investigator with the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could you give the Trial Chamber, please, a brief resume of all of your professional experience as an investigator, both at the Tribunal, but also your experience prior to coming to the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: I'm a Belgian, and I started to work in the Belgian Gendarmerie, National Police Force, back in June 1978. I stayed in the Gendarmerie for a bit more than 40 years until end of September 1982. And in October 1982, I joined the Judicial Police in Belgium, detective police force. I first worked as an inspector. And when I got promoted to the officer ranks in the Belgium police, I moved to the district of Leuven in '88 where I was the first year in charge of juvenile courts. And from '89, for the serious crimes part in the district of Leuven. Beginning of April 1995, I then joined the Tribunal as an investigator, and I got promoted to team leader -- investigations team leader of the Tribunal in March '97.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'll ask you just a couple of questions about your role as a team leader. Within the Office of the Prosecutor, perhaps you could describe for the Judges how the office is divided up in terms of the investigations which it conducts.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Well, we have a number of investigation teams, each in charge of an investigation, or more investigations eventually. Each investigation team is headed by a team leader, investigation team leader, who works alongside some lawyers, legal advisors who work on the team. Further on, the team is composed of investigators, crime analysts, translator or translators, and administrative support.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us just briefly what types of cases or investigations you have worked on during your time as an investigator with the office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Well, as an investigator, prior to becoming an investigation team leader - so from April '95 to March '97 - I worked in a team investigating mainly the sniping and shelling in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then you said you became a team leader in -- I believe in March of 1997. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And are you the leader of the investigative team which conducted the investigation in this case?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And are you familiar with the indictment in this case?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Yes, I am certainly familiar with the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Have you ever testified previously here at the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And when was that?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: It was in early July 1996; more than five years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What proceeding was that in which you testified?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: That was Rule 61 proceeding against Radovan Karadzic and Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did that relate to the -- your work on the siege of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I brought in evidence, the whole Sarajevo case, let's say, in sniping and shelling and the siege.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, in your capacity as the team leader or the team of the -- the leader of the investigative team in this case, beginning in March of 97, have you had an opportunity to visit and to conduct investigations in the places which are included or which are mentioned in the indictment in this case?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I went there on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And that includes Mostar, Sovici, Doljani, Siroki Brijeg, for example?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Yes, it includes all the places mentioned in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you also participate in interviews of witnesses who are expected to testify in this case?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then do you know whether other members of your investigations team conducted interviews as well under your direction?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, we are first going to start to go through and to show the Trial Chamber some images of many of the places which are alleged in the indictment. We are going to, with your permission, start out on a larger scale and slowly focus on the areas of particular relevance to this case. And I believe that the Registrar should have a binder for you, which is Binder 1, which is the same one that was distributed previously to the Judges. And I would ask that the Binder Number 1 be handed to the witnesses at this time. Mr. President, I was hoping that an easel would be available in the courtroom for this, but it's not here. I think that it's not necessary to really take a lot of time, but again this is just intended to orient the Trial Chamber in respect of the locations in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Van Hecke, if you could, what has been placed in front of the Judges is Exhibit P1, which is essentially a map of the entire former Yugoslavia. And it's a rather large map. And in order to move things along, rather than taking it out, I might just suggest that if you could approach this map, I'm going to ask you just to point out a number of locations for us just again so that we can be oriented. And first of all, if you could just give us an outline of the territory of what is now or what was in 1993 the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina on this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer, the problem is that we have to have it reflected in the transcript. Maybe could somebody say a few words about the scope of this area, so that it could be reflected in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I understand. Perhaps if -- I'm in your hands on how to proceed. I think the map, perhaps, speaks for itself. But what I could do is just give the microphone to Mr. Van Hecke, and he could perhaps make some statements about that, if that's acceptable to you.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Okay, this is the map of the Western Balkans published by The Times, and more or less in the middle of the map you can see the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then the Republic of Croatia was also mentioned in the Opening Statement. Could you just give us an idea of the positions now of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Yes. The republic is here, so north of Bosnia-Herzegovina and west of Bosnia-Herzegovina, so surrounding it from the north and the west.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Just looking at this map, could you give us a rough indication of the areas which are of relevance to this case, which are in Western Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Well, then we look to this area mainly in the southwestern corner of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the position of Zagreb, which was the capital -- is the capital of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Zagreb is here, in the north of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. And then finally in respect of Croatia, the position of a place called Split, which is a place some witnesses may talk about in this case.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Split is here on the Dalmatian Coast.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'm going to put what has been marked as Exhibit P3 in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Again, Mr. President, this was referred to by Mr. Scott in the opening statement. Maybe if I could ask the usher just to hold it up a little higher --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer, you have to use the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Microphone, you have to use the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Van Hecke, if you could just indicate, first of all, what this map is.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: This is the division of the territory into municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. And again, could you inform us, what is a municipality?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: A municipality is an administrative division of the country, and also the census of '91 was made according to the people in the municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And the municipalities involved in this case, again can you just give us a general idea of where they are located?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: They are located in this area on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. You can take your seat again now. And Mr. Van Hecke, the next exhibit I want to direct your attention to is in the binder. It's marked as Exhibit Number 2. Could you take that out, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, just for your information, this is the map that we're going to refer to quite frequently during the direct examination, and so it may be one that the Trial Chamber would like to keep closer at hand because it's this map that we're going to work on with the photographs and the videotapes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, on that subject of photos and videotapes, Mr. Van Hecke, are you aware that during the investigation in this case, members of your investigations team went into these areas and obtained photographs and videotaped images of the areas of relevance to this case?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And have you seen these photographs and videotapes, have you had an opportunity to review them?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, before we start looking at those, just to be clear, the conflict which is alleged in this case occurred in 1993. Is that when the photos and the videos were taken, or were they obtained at a later time?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: No, they were obtained many years later. So if I'm not mistaken, they are forensic missions, or photo missions, or video missions took place in September '99 and September of 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And finally, we're going to see some images taken from a helicopter. If you could just tell us how the team was able to obtain the helicopter and the services necessary to obtain that footage.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Well, to obtain this footage, we got logistical support from SFOR providing us with a helicopter and a helicopter crew, and we also got the assistance of a video team of the Dutch police to do that footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could you explain for us very briefly, what is SFOR?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: After the Dayton Agreements end of '95, NATO put an implementation force first into the country, IFOR. After a year, that was replaced by SFOR, so a NATO-led stabilisation force, which is an abbreviation, SFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The first locations that we're going to focus on are the places called Sovici and Doljani, and first of all, let me ask you if you're familiar with those two places and their relevance as alleged in the indictment in this case.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, for your information, if you wish - I'd be happy to, but certainly if you don't want me to, I won't - for each of these places, I can direct the Trial Chamber specifically to the relevant paragraphs of the indictment, which may assist in connecting the places to the indictment. Sovici is referred to, and Doljani, both are referred to in paragraph 9, the Background section of the indictment. They are both referred to in paragraph 25, which is part of Count 1 on persecution. Paragraph 46 refers to these places as part of the Counts 9 through 12 on torture and great suffering based on beatings of persons who were captured at Sovici and Doljani. Sovici and Doljani are also referred to in paragraph 53, which is part of Count 18, alleging the forcible transfer of civilians from their homes as a Grave Breach. And finally, Sovici and Doljani are alleged in paragraphs 55 and 56 of the indictment as places in which destruction occurred, devastation of homes and the mosque there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, if you could take Exhibit 2 out of the binder and place it on the ELMO. Just so we all know, indicate the location of Sovici and Doljani on this map, perhaps in relation to some of the larger places that are in the area.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: So here we have Sovici and Doljani. Jablanica is the closest town to the two villages of Doljani and Sovici, and they are both part of the municipality of Jablanica. Eastwards, you see Sarajevo, which is about 80 to 90 kilometres away from Jablanica. And Jablanica is on the main road from Sarajevo to Mostar, and you'll see Mostar approximately 40 kilometres south of Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. President, with your permission and hopefully with the assistance of our colleagues in the video booth, I have a videotape that shows Sovici. It's only about 60 to 90 seconds in length, and what I would propose to do is to show that video now - it's marked as Exhibit 4 - again just so you have an idea of what it looks like in these places.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Van Hecke, please feel free to give any commentary which might assist in understanding the layout.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Okay. As you see there, the village of Sovici and Doljani are in a valley northwest of Jablanica, so completely surrounded by the hills. This is a picture of the village of Sovici, going from east to west or from southeast to northwest. So Doljani and Jablanica would be on the right-hand side of the screen, more or less where the village of Sovici ends.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And am I correct that this particular photo is being taken from people who are standing on top of a hill, not from a helicopter?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Indeed, that's taken from the top of a hill, so going back from northwest to southeast over the village now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So this is panning from Sovici in the direction of Doljani?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know what that structure is there?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: That used to be the mosque of Sovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, Mr. Van Hecke, turning to the binder which is in front of you, could I ask you to look at Exhibit 6, which is a series of photographs. Have you had an opportunity to look over these photographs? And there is also a map which is on the front of those.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Yes, I had the opportunity.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And I want to ask you, if you could -- I've got two photographs, 6.7 and 6.9, which I could just ask the usher to place on the ELMO so you don't have to remove them. 6.7 first, can you tell us what is shown in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Well, you'll see part of Sovici in this photograph, and right here is the Sovici school.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And do you know the relevance of the Sovici school to the allegations which are alleged in the indictment in this case?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And just can you tell us what that's about?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: That's the place where, after taking over of the village by the HVO troops, people were imprisoned.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. And then quickly, Exhibit 6.9, a different photograph, just quickly tell us, what is Exhibit 6.9?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: That's a zoom-in of the school in Sovici right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. We can withdraw those --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer, you have to describe to us which building is that school. You know, you cannot only say, "This is the building of the school," so we could not find which one, you know. There should be some descriptions here of this particular place, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You're absolutely right, Mr. President, and I apologise. I think after you've seen so many of these photographs a hundred times, you don't think about it anymore, and that's my fault.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Van Hecke, maybe if you can describe the building which you're saying is the Sovici school, for the record.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: You want me to do it on 6.7 or 6.9?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: 6.7 is on the ELMO. You can use 6.7.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: So approximately just above the middle of the photograph, we see a long, wide building with a red roof, and that's the Sovici school on Exhibit 6.7.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then in 6.9, just quickly take us to 6.9.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: So on 6.9, exactly in the middle of the photo, we see again the same long, wide building with the red roof, being the Sovici school.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Van Hecke. And now that was Sovici. The next place is Doljani. And again if you could just come back to Exhibit 2, just to refresh us in terms of the location of the village of Doljani.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: So again when we see the map and we see the municipality of Jablanica north of the centre of the map, you'll see the town of Jablanica marked in red on the map. And northwest of it, next to the border with the municipality of Prozor, you have first Doljani and then Sovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. President, with your permission, I propose to show another short videotape which gives images of the village of Doljani. That would be Exhibit Number 7.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: So this helicopter footage, east is again -- right is east and left is west. The helicopter is turning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The place that's now being shown, which appears to be a fish farm, or a pisces kultura, can you describe the relevance of that to the case?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Witnesses have told us that this was the headquarters of Naletilic, Tuta, during --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: May it please the Tribunal, the Defence for Mr. Naletilic would have to object to this witness's testimony, other than what he observed from the documentation and not any other evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Again, if you could just continue with describing what you're saying perhaps for the moment, Mr. Van Hecke. If you could --

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Well, we see the village of Doljani, with the big building which you see is a school in Doljani. This road going up is the road going to Sovici, further up in the valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What direction are we moving now along this road?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Well, roughly said, northwest.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: In the direction from, say, what place to what place?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Well, if you take the road back, you would be in Jablanica, so down. And then if we follow here, through Doljani and further on to Sovici up in the valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. President, just on the last question, I'm not sure exactly that I understand the basis of the objection. I think we're simply trying to make a connection between places which are being shown and the allegations in the indictment. I think the witness is in a position to do that. If he is going to make statements or give a statement about what he's learned in the course of the investigation, it may, in fact, be hearsay. But I think that it's admissible, because there's not a strict ban on hearsay here. I don't suggest that Mr. Van Hecke's testimony is the only testimony that you should consider. I think, in fact, without testimony of the witnesses to say these things, it has and should have very little effect on you. So I think that I would propose to try to ask Mr. Van Hecke to simply say if he's aware what is the relevance of this or that place to the charges in the indictment, simply as a way to draw a connection between what we're seeing and in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think I should ask Mr. Meek to explain what the objection is. You know, I don't quite understand what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, if it please the Tribunal --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Meek, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I apologise. If it please the Tribunal, there is earlier testimony in the first tape of Sovici and unsolicited statements by this witness concerning events which he claims happened. This witness was not present in 1993, in April of that year, when the events that are alleged in this indictment occurred. That is my objection, Your Honour. I understand that hearsay may and is admissible. However, I do not believe that conclusions, bare conclusions or opinions, are appropriate for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stringer, do you have any reaction to this objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I think that the witness is in a position, as the lead case agent, to simply say how a particular place relates to what is alleged in the indictment. I don't mean to suggest that his statements on that should be dispositive and should be relied upon by the Trial Chamber as substantive evidence that you would be relying on as part of a verdict or a judgement in this case. He's familiar with the investigation, he's familiar with the indictment, and if he's in a position because of that to simply inform you how a particular place relates to allegations contained in the indictment, I believe that he ought to be able to simply draw that connection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Meek, I think the witness is trying to lead us into the particular locations of this case. Of course he was not present at the spot area where the alleged crime was committed, but even the hearsay evidence has some probative values before this Tribunal. So your objection is overruled. Please continue, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And continuing with Doljani, first of all, I'm not certain that the Trial Chamber had a sufficient opportunity to view the videotape because objections were made. We could replay it if you wish, Mr. President, or I could move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Van Hecke, then, for Doljani I directed your attention in the binder to a series of photographs marked as Exhibit Number 8. Have you had an opportunity to review these photographs? And if so, tell us what they are.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Yes, I had the opportunity to review these photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And what are these photographs?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: These photographs show the valley where Doljani is located, gives general overviews of the village of Doljani, showed the destroyed school. And I'm pointing at Exhibit 8.4.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Let me just move you through. I would ask the usher to show you two photographs on the ELMO, 8.8 and 8.9. Can you, Mr. Van Hecke, can you simply tell us the relevance of this place as alleged in the indictment, if you're in a position to say so?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Well, we see on this Exhibit 8.8 a building with some water in front. This is a fish farm in Doljani alleged to be Mr. Naletilic's headquarters in April 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. And then in Photograph Number 8.9?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: That's again the same two buildings with the water in front, so again the fish farm, but more zoomed in.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in some of the other photographs, there's one thing I think we should be clear about, in terms of events in Doljani. There are houses and there is a fair amount of destruction that is indicated in the photographs. The indictment in this case alleges events which occurred in Sovici and Doljani in April of 1993. Are you aware of subsequent military operations which occurred in that same area subsequently during 1993?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Yes. There was a main attack from the AbiH or army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, a counterattack at the end of July of 1993, so some of this destruction you see did not necessarily happen during April of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Just so it's clear, Mr. President -- well, I'll ask it as a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Since you're familiar with the indictment, does the indictment allege that Mr. Naletilic is responsible for destruction which occurred during July of 1993?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: No, he's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Moving forward, Mr. President, we're now going to take a look at the city of Mostar. We can withdraw these two photos from the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And again coming back to the map which is Exhibit Number 2, so we can just get an idea of the location of Mostar perhaps now in reference to Sovici and Doljani, where is Mostar located?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: So again we have here Sovici/Doljani as pointed out before on this map. From Sovici, I estimate it's approximately 12, 13 kilometres to Jablanica. And Jablanica, you come back on the main road from Sarajevo to Mostar, going down south. So from Jablanica south on the main road, about 40 kilometres south, you reach the city of Mostar, so just under the middle of the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. President, Mostar, coming back to the indictment, Mostar is referred to in many places in the indictment. I could go through each of those if you wish, but I can say generally that Mostar -- the significance of Mostar is the fact that it's the confrontation line and crimes which occurred in the confrontation line as alleged in Count 1, paragraph 32, and in Counts 2 through 8, paragraph 54, and also the forcible transfer of civilians from West Mostar across the confrontation line into East Mostar, which is alleged in paragraph 54 of the indictment as part of Count 18. Now, we have a videotape image of the confrontation line in Mostar, which is marked as Exhibit Number -- I'm sorry, I'm getting ahead of myself, Mr. President. I first am going to ask Mr. Van Hecke to look at what's been marked as Exhibit Number 11, which is a map of the Mostar centrum or the centre of the city, which was relied on in reference by Mr. Scott during his Opening Statement, because with the assistance of Exhibit P11, I want to ask Mr. Van Hecke some questions. And perhaps if we could put that on the ELMO, it would assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: First of all, Mr. Van Hecke, let me ask you: This map, did you prepare this map or did you have any involvement in the preparation of this?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Have you had an opportunity to review the map?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And using this map, if you would, based on the allegations in the indictment, could you tell us perhaps a little bit about the layout of Mostar and point out some of the areas on the map which are of relevance to the indictment in this case.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Well, again when we see the map, the north is to the right and the south to the left. So up is in the west, of course, and down the east. Mostar is positioned around the Neretva River flowing through the town of Mostar, and basically the area under the Neretva in this case, so east of the Neretva or east of Mostar is basically part of the Muslim area or was part of the Muslim area in Mostar. They were the position more up or above the Neretva River along the west side, also called the right bank of the river because the river is flowing south. It was mixed at the time before the conflict and had mainly Croat but quite a significant presence of Bosniaks too.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Just for the record now, you're indicating the Neretva River, which is flowing from right to left as we look at the screen, and then so on the top or the west side is which side again?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Mainly Croat side.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. With a Muslim population?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: With a Muslim population, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then below the river or east, the east side of the river again?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Is mainly a Muslim population or Bosniak population.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, the indictment in this case makes reference on a number of occasions to the confrontation line in Mostar, and with this map, if you could, just indicate the location of the confrontation line as it's alleged in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: So under the big yellow part, which is a mountain, a hill overlooking Mostar, you see a street called "Bulevar," so the confrontation line mainly followed the Bulevar all the way along. Then you see a square called "Spanske Drug" [phonetic], so the "Spanish Square." Continue it a little bit further in the first narrow street then to the right, continue the confrontation line, and then to go to Aleksa Santic Street, almost to the end, and then go through the buildings to the direction of Carinski Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, so that generally speaking, the area in yellow gives an indication of the location of the confrontation line in --

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Yes, just an indication of the confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, can you just tell us where the two opposing sides were positioned in the area of this confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Well, in the case of this map, the HVO was positioned on the top side of the Bulevar, and then Santiceva Street or Aleksa Santic Street. The armija AbiH forces were positioned on this map just under the Bulevar, so they were -- the confrontation line was where these two streets, the Bulevar and Santiceva Street, just facing each other with a few metres difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. So then the armija had this small area of terrain on the west side of the Neretva river?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Indeed, there was an AbiH-held enclave on the western bank or right bank of the river.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I think with that introduction, Mr. President, we could play the videotape, which has been marked Exhibit Number 13. And I would again ask Mr. Van Hecke, if he could, as the videotape plays, just to indicate for us how some of the locations on the videotape relate to locations indicated on Exhibit Number 11.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: So again, you see an overfly of Mostar. The green part on top is mound that I spoke to you about earlier, with the Bulevar, the roads just going under the mounds. So you are going -- the Bulevar is going from south to north, being the confrontation line at the time. So the helicopter is now turning to go straight north. On the top here, you see that building which is the house of health, goes straight to the left. On the right-hand side, you see the buildings where the armija positions. On the left-hand side were the HVO positions. So you are following the Bulevar. You see the difference between the lines was like 15 metres only. The big building you see on the left-hand side of the screen is the gymnasium of the school. On the right-hand top, you see the toll bridge. Here, that narrow street that is at the middle of the screen now was in front of the confrontation line. And then going left through that rather narrow street, which is Aleksa Santic Street. And then at the end, going through the buildings mainly, which is another direct straight line to the next bit that you see, Sarintska...

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. President, we have a series of photographs which come from that videotape which we could now look at, which would, I think, again, make it a little easier to tie locations down.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I direct your attention, Mr. Van Hecke, to Exhibit Number 14, a series of photographs within the binder. And I'm first going to ask you to look at Exhibit Number 14.3. Okay, now, with the pointer, Mr. Van Hecke, you made a reference to the health centre, I believe. And you also made a reference to the gymnasium or the gymnasium. Can you, on the ELMO, point to those two places and describe for the record where they are located.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: I am pointing now to the house of health, Dom Zdravnja, which is located on the photo a bit higher up from the middle of the centre of the photo. It's a pink building, a bit special shape building, at the junction between the two streets.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then the gymnasium?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: The gymnasium is the big building here at the bottom of the photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Maybe, Mr. President, for the record, I could ask the witness simply to circle those two places. We could put some letters next to them so that the record would indicate more clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Van Hecke, could you put a circle around what you are calling the health centre. And you could write next to that HC, for Health Centre. And then if you could circle the gymnasium. Thank you. Now, if you could, Mr. Van Hecke, what I would like to do very quickly, going back to Exhibit Number 11, which is the map that we were just looking at, can you show us the location of these two places on Exhibit Number 11, just again so we are able to make the connection between these two.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: The place number 1 is the -- the place number 1 is a health centre, and the place marked as number 2 is the gymnasium.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Number 1 and number 2, you are referring to as on Exhibit Number P11?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And on the photograph, which is now on the ELMO again, those same two places on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. So the one I circled, the pink building is the health centre. The big one on the bottom of the photo is the gymnasium.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Now, the next photograph would be Exhibit 14.5. If you would turn to that one, again, if you could just briefly describe the place that's indicated in 14.5.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Well, again, we see the health centre here in the centre of the photo. And in front of it, the fountain just at the junction of the two streets here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Are you aware of -- the indictment makes allegations about this location. Do you know what those allegations are?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could you tell us briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: It's alleged that Mr. Martinovic had commanded some of his people from that centre, and also incidents that actually happened on the 17th of September happened in the neighbourhood of this place.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: 17th of September?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, in the indictment, that would go back to paragraph 41 and 42, events of the 17th of September, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Van Hecke, the next photo is 14.7. Just again, briefly, now, if you could give us an indication, generally, what this place is.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Well, you see an overview of the Bulevar, looking from north to south. So on the left-hand side of the photo, you see the positions at the time held by the AbiH. On the right-hand side of the street, you see the positions held by the HVO. And at the back of the photo, you see a mountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And the next is 14.7. Was that 7? 14.17. Can you tell us what this area is and perhaps how it relates to Exhibit Number P11, which is the map.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: What you see on the -- it's the top right of the photo. First you see the Neretva River, the very top right, Neretva River. And then the first real street you see with all the damaged houses, that's Aleksa Santic Street, which is let's say the continuation of the confrontation line after the Bulevar in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could you just quickly show us that same location where it would be found on Exhibit P11.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Yes, that would be here. So the place that you see as Number 6 on this map is this big building here, which is Hotel Ero. So the street goes from the top of 14.7 to the right, and that's this street marked in yellow on Exhibit 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay, so essentially 14.17 indicates the area of the Aleksa Santic Street indicated on P11.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then 14.19, please. I am skipping one, just to... If you could quickly indicate what's shown in 14.19.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Well, that's again the same street now taken from -- photo taken from the other direction, so from the east side of Mostar. Here, you again see, from left to right, Aleksa Santic Street. You still see a lot of destruction there as a result of the warfare.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Then at the very bottom left-hand corner of the photo, the bottom left-hand corner of the photo.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Yes, you see Neretva River.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, it's 4:00. I'm ready to move to the next location, or we can break, as you wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will adjourn until 9:30 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 11th day of September, 2001, at 9.30 a.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: ---  Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.00 p.m.,
